data.copy:
Chapter One
Silas: I don’t know how much they paid you but this should be more than enough to keep your mouth shut. If you try to contact me…If I hear one word about this from anyone…It’ll be the last thing anybody will ever hear from you.
Slam!
* * *
Echo of the slamming door woke Lynn from her restless sleep. Ten years and it still affected her. Ten years and she recalled every detail as if it were yesterday no matter how she tried to forget. The day she finally faced her high school crush…the day he broke her heart and her world fell apart.
Ten years ago Avalynn Carlisle was the younger of two daughters born to Emerson and Grace Carlisle. Her sister Marilynn was a true beauty queen: tall and confident. Avalynn meanwhile was plain, petite and quiet. She could never network or socialize the way her sister could having only one close friend throughout primary school. There was only one area Avalynn truly shined and that was music.
Since she was five and had her first piano lesson her instructors praised her as a rare genius, gifted. When she played the rest of the world ceased to exist. It was just her and the music. She was hailed as a prodigy and every party her parents hosted she played for their guests. Little did she realize this scant attention was enough to stoke her sister’s jealousy.
Shortly after graduation Avalynn won a coveted spot at Julliard. Her sister insisted they go out and celebrate despite the fact Avalynn never drank before. She didn’t know what alcohol was supposed to be like and she never suspected her sister would drug her or that Marilynn would throw her into bed with an unknown man. But that is exactly what her sister did.
Mercifully the event was blocked by a fog and Ava had no recollection of the act itself. The next morning was traumatic enough. She woke with a pounding headache, intense thirst and incredibly sore. Completely wear nothing with something running between her l…

“And you allowed this?” he demanded. “Your own granddaughter? For ten years I came to you with worry over my daughter and you wouldn’t tell me?”
“You wouldn’t accept the mates I had for her!” the Beta shouted back.
“They were centuries old, men who’d already had and lost their mates! I thought she had yet to find her own! But you knew all along.”
“She’s human!”
“So is her grandmother!”
“But she wasn’t born of werewolves. How many other were born humans have you heard of?” he answered his own question. “None.”
“The alpha line has to he be strong son, you know that.” her grandmother rationalized.
————————
Pain once again scored through her, a tearing inside her that seemed to encompass all her soul. It felt like claws were raking through her stomach while another set shredded her heart. At the same time, the essence of who she was was being dragged out of her with the most exquisite pain there ever had been, slowly. It was unbearable but she’d had to bear it, had survived it for so long.

With her father holding tightly to her, the storm finally eased until all she felt were the after-effects. The numbing ache that she could only combat by being as still as possible. Tears still flowed down her cheeks but now she could hear what her father whispered against her hair as his own tears wet her dark strands. It broke her heart, worse knowing she was causing his pain.

“I’m so sorry I failed you...” he whispered to her still form. “...sweet baby girl...failed you...should’ve seen...should’ve protected you...baby girl, forgive me.”

Her dad was a strong man. A man who never cried but because of her, he was. Because of her, he sounded broken. Why couldn’t she have been born stronger? Or not at all?

data.caption: 20min Bedtimes in 14 Days Or Your Don't Pay
data.copy:
From 3 hour bedtime battles with my kid to 22mins in 14 days after 5 years. 

This used to take us 3 hours. I'm not exaggerating.

7:30pm: "Time for bed!" 10:30pm: Still negotiating, still chasing, still losing my mind.

Every. Single. Night.

I tried the weighted blanket (kicked off by 9pm, too hot anyway).

I tried melatonin (helped him fall asleep, didn't help him STAY asleep).

I tried the strict routine, the no-screens rule, the calm music, the lavender spray, the magnesium gummies.

I tried yelling. I tried crying. I tried bribing.

Nothing worked.

My husband and I hadn't had a conversation that wasn't about bedtime in months. My other daughter started asking why I was "always grumpy." I was running on 5 hours of broken sleep and pretending I was fine.

I wasn't fine.

Then I found out WHY nothing was working
.
Turns out, my son's brain wasn't being difficult. It was missing something. Something every other "sleep solution" completely ignores.

That's when I found the NeuroNest Sleep Cocoon.

It's not a weighted blanket. It's not another supplement. 

It's 360° compression designed specifically for ADHD and neurodivergent kids — and it works all night because they actually wear it.

Now bedtime looks like that picture on the right. 20 minutes. Peaceful. Done.

No more negotiations. No more hallway camping. No more 10pm exhaustion spirals.

They're running a Buy One, Get One 50% OFF sale right now (I grabbed a backup for grandma's house).
